newsitem.title: UK: European debt futures felled by U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: European debt futures felled by U.S. data.

text.p: European debt futures took a dive on Friday as a slew of U.S. inflation and sales data sparked confused trade in the pits.
Initially Bund futures on LIFFE took March's U.S. producer price figures well, giving bulls sufficient head to push the market higher. But the retail sales data gave bears the sway.
"Half (the traders) went one way and half the other," said a trader at a U.S. bank on the LIFFE floor.
U.S. producer prices fell 0.1 percent in March compared with a 0.4 percent drop in February. Core PPI rose 0.4 percent versus a 0.1 percent fall in the previous month.
March retail sales rose a lower than expected 0.2 percent, compared to a revised 1.5 percent increase in February.
At 1321 GMT June Bunds were trading down 12 basis points at 99.99, off from 100.31 before the data.
The June notionnel contract on the MATIF was down 12 basis points at 128.22, versus 128.50 before the data, and British gilts on LIFFE were off 6/32 at 108-23, from 109-05 before.
"It's a sign people were short the market and made a dash for cover," said a French bank trader. "It's still trying to find a base and hold there."
Traders said when the T-bond future dipped through 106-28, that undermined the Bunds. June T-bonds were trading down 25/32 at 106-18.
"Bund stops started going off all over the place," said the French trader.
Bund traders said the market was eyeing support at 99.80 in late trade.
